clue.text: Boycott? Ought to put in cooler!

indicators.note: the clue tells us to put one piece inside another, the word for cooler being opened up

parts.note: cooler means colder
ought to means should

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a boycotter, perhaps cricketer Geoffrey Boycott, gets locked up in jail ('the cooler').
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boycott?' looks like the cricketer's name but is the definition; 'cooler' is slang for prison in the surface but here simply means colder.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the snub, deliberately ignoring them, is to boycott them socially.

clue.text: European visiting revolutionary South American city for so long

indicators.note: visiting means staying among, so the European letter sits between the other pieces

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary
Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, is called Rio

explanation.surface: A European spends a long time in a city linked with a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual British farewell, like saying goodbye or so long.

clue.text: Novelist giving thanks for opening book being ignored

indicators.note: being ignored means left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a blessing is a grace or thanks said before a meal

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word book

explanation.surface: A novelist gives thanks when the start of a book is overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing was a British Nobel-winning author of novels such as The Golden Notebook.

clue.text: Stark quality of Kentish Town

definitions.meaning: the state of being sheer, utter or absolute
a port town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent

explanation.surface: Kentish Town is a district of London, with a quality of starkness.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a real London district, but here it means a town in Kent, the English county south-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means absolute, so the abstract noun is utterness; it is also a Kent port.

clue.text: Bird left to go south of river

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means placed below, so the left letter comes after

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A bird leaves the north and heads south of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Also spelt ouzel, it is an old name for the blackbird or ring ouzel.

clue.text: Arriving by jet leaving France, being lazy

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter for France is removed

parts.note: arriving by plane is flying in
F is the international abbreviation for France

explanation.surface: Someone flies in after leaving France and feels idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed late in the morning is a lazy act.

clue.text: Turkish official fed fine cooking

indicators.note: cooking suggests something being cooked up or altered, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A Turkish dignitary is fed some fine cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: A title of respect for a man of standing or government officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Bear with Barker — Corbett had a hand in this popular duo

definitions.text: Bear with Barker — Corbett had a hand in this popular duo

parts.words: Bear with Barker — Corbett had a hand in this popular duo
parts.note: a yellow glove-puppet bear and his dog friend, worked by the hand of Harry Corbett and later his son Matthew

explanation.surface: It reads like a comic duo with Ronnie Barker and Ronnie Corbett.
explanation.walkthrough: Barker and Corbett suggest The Two Ronnies, but 'Barker' is a dog and Corbett is the puppeteer who literally had his hand in the puppets of this long-running British children's TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous British children's TV glove puppets, a bear and a dog, are this pair.

clue.text: Hold chap directed over a national leader

parts.note: a nelson is a wrestling hold
a chap is a man

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: directed means led

explanation.surface: A man is held and directed over a national leader.
explanation.definitionFit: He was South Africa's first black president, a national leader after apartheid.

clue.text: Manage love poetry before 'East is East'

indicators.note: before places the poetry ahead of the compass point in the answer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
poetry is verse

explanation.surface: A quotation from Kipling ('East is East...') seems to be tacked onto a direction about love poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase is decoration: 'East is' acts as a link meaning East is represented, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or direct something is to manage it.

clue.text: Boat the French folk rock, Fifties-style

parts.note: a skiff is a small rowing boat
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A French boat seems to be rocking, set in the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: Skiffle was a 1950s British craze of folk-blues music played on homemade instruments such as the washboard.
explanation.definitionFit: This music genre blended folk and early rock-and-roll during the Fifties.

clue.text: Bank admits blunder getting part-timer in Services

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the bank word holds the blunder word inside it

parts.note: a bank of seats is a tier
to blunder is to err

explanation.surface: A bank lets in a mistaken applicant who works part-time for the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: A Terrier is informal British for a member of the Territorial Army, the part-time volunteer reserve of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Territorial Army's volunteers were nicknamed after this word, as reservists serving part-time.

clue.text: People admired those at the bottom of the table

definitions.meaning: famous, much-admired figures are called greats or icons

definitions.text: those at the bottom of the table
definitions.meaning: the explanatory keys or captions printed under a table or chart

explanation.surface: Admired people sit at the bottom of a league table, a sporting irony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' suggests a league table, but here it is a printed chart whose key or caption sits beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated heroes are so called, and so are captions or keys explaining a chart or map.

clue.text: By the side of a pine

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Something stands next to a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree but is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking beside a river is walking parallel to it, a sense of this preposition.

clue.text: Old partner criticises one about getting fatter

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
one is the Roman numeral I
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A former spouse mocks someone for putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Growth in size, such as a waistline swelling, is a kind of enlargement.

clue.text: Clergy generally assembled at seaport

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Clergymen are gathered at a seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastors as a body, or the office of pastor, form this collective noun.

clue.text: She cussed degenerate aristocrats

indicators.note: degenerate suggests things falling into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman swore at a group of decadent nobles.
explanation.definitionFit: Wives of dukes, or female holders of ducal titles, are high-ranking nobility.

clue.text: Empty box, apparently? One may find it funny

indicators.note: apparently signals a whimsical reading: a box with nothing inside is a box holding the zero letter

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard box
empty means containing nothing, and nothing is O

explanation.surface: An empty box is offered as something amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'empty box' is taken literally as a box with nothing (O) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous drawing or animated film is designed to make people laugh.

clue.text: Lace drink? You'll need hospital department first

indicators.note: first places the department ahead of the drink

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Spiking a drink? Better get the hospital involved first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lace' suggests spiking a drink, but here means twine together.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace threads together is to twist or weave them around each other.

clue.text: What to perform in humdrum ballroom

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice on which dance to perform in a dull ballroom.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban ballroom dance is something one performs on the dance floor.

clue.text: Musical performance playing clarinet, not new

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played with and rearranged
not means without, so the letter for new is removed

explanation.surface: A musical performance on a clarinet that is not new.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo concert by a performer or small group is this kind of event.

clue.text: More substantial area covered by what one's good at

indicators.note: covered by means placed inside, so the area letter is enclosed

parts.note: one's metier is one's forte

explanation.surface: A large area is covered by someone's speciality.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaty means having substance, so its comparative is weightier.

clue.text: Beat material

definitions.meaning: beaten or defeated in a contest
a fine woollen yarn or fabric

explanation.surface: Two bare words: a thrashing and some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A past-tense verb meaning defeated, and a smooth woollen cloth named after a Norfolk village.

clue.text: Speech must be given with no notice, in costume

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the notice letters are removed

parts.note: an address is a formal speech
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A speech must be given at short notice by someone in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no notice' suggests short notice, but it removes AD (an advert).
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing, especially a particular style of attire, is a synonym for outfit.

clue.text: Where to grow fruit or vegetable

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether to plant fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed plot of fruit trees is the place apples and pears are raised.

clue.text: Showing feelings I have after upsetting book

indicators.note: after places the contracted words behind the turned book
upsetting in a down-to-earth sense means overturning, so the book word is turned round

parts.note: a tome is a large book
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone shows emotion after reading a distressing book.
explanation.definitionFit: Language that stirs or expresses strong emotions is described this way.

clue.text: A number, unspecified, work round hospital, bustling place

parts.note: n stands for an unspecified number in maths

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the work word encloses the hospital letter

parts.note: to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: Some number of people work around a hospital, which is a busy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts H inside TILL, giving THILL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ants' nest heaps up with constant activity, so it stands for any busy, crowded place.

clue.text: Command to infiltrate alien terrains in the realm of Star Trek

definitions.text: in the realm of Star Trek

indicators.note: to infiltrate means to get inside, so the command word goes within the rearranged letters
alien means strange or foreign, so the letters are made strange by rearrangement

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to command them

explanation.surface: An order is given to invade alien landscapes, as in a Star Trek episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alien' looks like a Star Trek creature but signals the anagram; 'to infiltrate' places the command inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek's voyages take place between the stars, out in deep space.
